decisions.reason: The literal É-accent derivation does not alter the Hero V geometry; the candidate already identifies the approved Option 2 geometry as the foundation.
The new literal-derivation rule applies specifically to the É accent. The closing V remains derived from the Hero V geometry under its existing rule.

The client strengthens the shared terminal treatment by requiring the É accent to be the literal terminal section of the approved Hero V right arm while retaining one unified gesture across all three glyphs.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Thank you for putting the family together. Seeing the capital V, lowercase v, and É accent together is exactly the right next step, and I think it confirms that we're now refining an architectural language rather than an individual letter.

One thing also became very clear to me. The hero V is still Option 2 from the previous round (attaching here for reference). I think that silhouette remains the strongest foundation, and I'd love to continue building the system from that version rather than the updated hero V in this presentation.

Looking at the family together also gave me another important realization. I don't want the É accent to simply be inspired by the hero V—I want it to literally be the termination of the hero V.

If you could imagine taking the last portion of the hero V's right arm, lifting it off the letter, and placing it above the É, that's the relationship I'm looking for. To me, those should be the exact same gesture. I think that consistency is what will make the identity feel truly proprietary.

I'd love to continue refining the system with that idea in mind. Once that gesture feels completely unified across the capital V, lowercase v, and É accent, I think we'll have found something really special.

value_updates.terminal_role: Exact same signature gesture unified across the Hero V, second V, and É accent, with the É accent literally formed from the terminal section of the approved Hero V right arm

decisions.reason: The decision concerns the É accent and V-system gesture, not the supporting E and L letterform construction.
Requiring a unified terminal gesture does not change the closing V's smaller, subordinate visual prominence.
The glyph-derivation decision does not change the obligation to provide design rationale with review rounds.
The literal accent derivation changes geometry, not the deferred champagne material treatment.
The relationship between the Hero V terminal and É accent does not alter the deferred full-wordmark kerning requirement.
